title: MSW v2 export resolution and fetch polyfills under Jest JSDOM
answers: Why does MSW fail to resolve or intercept requests in frontend Jest tests?
Why does PostHog use a custom Jest resolver in frontend/jest.resolver.js?
Where are fetch and Web Stream polyfills loaded for Jest in frontend/?
body:
Running MSW v2 inside Jest JSDOM breaks unless both export resolution and polyfill loading order are specifically handled:
- Package resolution: Under JSDOM's default `browser` condition, MSW v2 and its `@mswjs/*` dependencies define Node subpath exports as `null`. `frontend/jest.resolver.js:MSW_ECOSYSTEM` intercepts package names starting with `msw` or `@mswjs/` and forces Jest's default resolver to use `conditions: ['node', 'require', 'import']`.
- Fetch primitives: JSDOM lacks or alters spec-compliant fetch primitives. `frontend/jest.polyfills.js` must execute first in `setupFiles` to bind `ReadableStream`, `WritableStream`, `Response`, `Request`, `Headers`, and `fetch` from `undici` to `globalThis` before test suites boot.
applies: Only for MSW v2 and packages in the `@mswjs/` ecosystem running in Jest with JSDOM; standard frontend browser packages use default JSDOM resolution.
says: Simulated network requests fail to intercept during frontend component test execution
Automated interface tests crash with missing web stream and request primitives
Frontend test runner cannot resolve network mock dependencies properly in tests
Network mocking setup causes frontend unit test suites to fail prematurely
